root_cause.text: In `fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()`, the code unconditionally incremented the `nfs4_file` access count via `__nfs4_file_get_access()` even when `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` had already been installed by another thread, causing a leaked `fi_access` reference that prevented the associated `nfsd_file` from being freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `__nfs4_file_get_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ);` inside `if (!fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY])` and the commit message says that “if fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is already set by another thread, __nfs4_file_get_access should not be called” because the “extra fi_access count in nfs4_file can prevent the corresponding nfsd_file from being freed,” leading to `kmem_cache_destroy()` BUGs on shutdown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Move read-access and delegation-file setup under the O_RDONLY initialization check so they only run when a new read file is installed.
intent_record.what: Inside nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg(), the call to __nfs4_file_get_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ) was moved from before the conditional block to inside the !fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] branch, and the assignment to fp->fi_rdeleg_file was moved into that same branch immediately after fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is set to nf.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the read-access accounting and setting of the read-delegation file now happen only when the O_RDONLY file slot is actually being initialized. This avoids incrementing access state and updating fi_rdeleg_file when an O_RDONLY file already exists, aligning the bookkeeping with the actual state transition.

grouping_result.intent: Move read-access and delegation-file setup under the O_RDONLY initialization check so they only run when a new read file is installed.

relevance_review.reason: The change matches the root cause directly: it prevents read-access/delegation setup from running when O_RDONLY was already installed, avoiding the extra fi_access increment and the resulting leaked reference.

candidates.rationale: This access-count increment was executed unconditionally, even when O_RDONLY was already installed by another thread. That could leak a fi_access reference and prevent the nfsd_file from being freed.

This was also performed outside the O_RDONLY initialization check, so it could run even when no new read file was installed, contributing to incorrect reference handling tied to the leaked access reference.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line unconditionally increments the nfs4_file access count even when another thread has already installed fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY], which leaks a fi_access reference and can prevent the associated nfsd_file from being freed.

This statement was executed outside the O_RDONLY initialization check, so it could run even when no new read file was installed, contributing to the incorrect reference handling associated with the leaked access count.

Author: Chuck Lever <chuck.lever@oracle.com>
Date:   Mon Dec 1 17:09:55 2025 -0500

    nfsd: fix nfsd_file reference leak in nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()
    
    nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg() unconditionally overwrites
    fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] with a newly acquired nfsd_file. However, if
    the client already has a SHARE_ACCESS_READ open from a previous OPEN
    operation, this action overwrites the existing pointer without
    releasing it
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already contains the fix for the reported leak. In the vulnerable version, `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] = nf;` and `fp->fi_rdeleg_file = nf;` were done unconditionally after `__nfs4_file_get_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ);`, which could overwrite an existing `O_RDONLY` file pointer and leak the old reference. Here the code checks `if (!fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]) { fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] = nf; nf = NULL; }` and then assigns `fp->fi_rdeleg_file = nfsd_file_get(fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]);`, followed by `if (nf) nfsd_file_put(nf);`. This avoids overwriting an existing `O_RDONLY` entry without dropping its reference and ensures the delegation file gets its own reference, so the vulnerable construct is no longer present.
